intent.note: Clause 'Compare the file's raw bytes with what checkout itself would write, `git cat-file --filters <commit>:<rel>`' - diff: plugins/audit/scripts/git/_worktrees.py _reads_as now runs `_git_bytes(tree, ["cat-file", "--filters", "%s:%s" % (commit, rel)])` and returns `fh.read() == checked_out` (file opened 'rb'), replacing `hash-object --no-filters`. Clause 'Add a variant of un5 that sets core.autocrlf=true, checks out the head, and expects the file to read as the commit's' - diff: un11 (tests/test__worktrees.py _autocrlf_cases) sets core.autocrlf=true, removes and re-checks-out c.txt, asserts the on-disk bytes are CRLF and _reads_as is True, with LF-only and foreign-bytes twins False. un12/un13 go past the clause to the consequence it names ('no verb can settle the tree'): restore_copy and the next advance_task_tree settle a move killed mid-checkout under autocrlf. The un5 core.eol=lf pin is a necessary consequence: with `*.txt text` and core.eol native, Git for Windows checks out CRLF, so under the new comparison un5's two halves invert on windows; the pin fixes the fixture, it does not hide a behaviour - on a native-CRLF checkout the CRLF file IS checkout's bytes and the LF file is the line-ending edit, which is exactly what the new comparison reports, and the CRLF-writing conversion path is exercised by un11 (autocrlf=true and eol=crlf both reach git's output-eol conversion; probed: `cat-file --filters` under `*.txt text` + core.eol=crlf printed x\r\n). The pin relies on the sweep's isolated git config (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, runner-owned global): a direct run on a windows host whose system config sets core.autocrlf=true would override core.eol and redden un5, but the suite's other checkout-byte cases already assume that isolation. Windows correctness: Git for Windows writes stdout in binary mode and Python's PIPE is bytes, and the file is read 'rb', so no translation sits on either side; `_git_bytes` keeps stdout undecoded for exactly this read and `_git` keeps its prior signature and decoded shape. .gitattributes: `cat-file --filters` applies smudge, ident, working-tree-encoding and eol under the tree's own config and attributes, the same convert-to-worktree path checkout uses. One residual, fail-closed: cat-file reads .gitattributes from the working tree, while a multi-file checkout prefers the index's, so when a move changes .gitattributes AND is killed before the new attributes file is written, a moved path can read as differing and the tree is held for a human - the pre-fix outcome, never a reset of someone's edit. Smudge filters (e.g. LFS) now run on this read; under the old comparison such files never matched at all. Claim: the executor's outcome describes the diff as it stands - _git as `_git_bytes` plus the same decode, rev-parse still through the injected runner and the content read through `_git_bytes` (said in the docstring; production callers in drive-phase.py inject no runner), drive-phase.py and tests/test_drive_phase.py unchanged, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's sentence replaced to name cat-file --filters and un11-un13.
